$comment: Per-project unit-test coverage floors enforced by scripts/check-coverage.mjs.
These are RATCHET FLOORS, not targets. Each floor is the coverage the project
actually had when it was last baselined, minus a ~2 point buffer. Raise a floor
whenever a project's real coverage moves above it; never lower one to make CI green.
The Beta target under negotiation (NXENG-615 asks for >90% everywhere) is tiered:
90% on new library services and the agent gateway, 70% on feature components with
logic. See AGENTS/05-test-standards.md.
DENOMINATOR DEFECT FIXED — 2026-08-06. The gate used to read v8's project total, and
v8 only instruments files a test run loads: a source file no spec imported contributed
zero lines to the total instead of counting as uncovered, so it vanished from the
denominator rather than dragging the percentage down. Reported coverage was inflated
and the incentive inverted — the first engineer to write a spec that loaded a large
untested file made measured coverage FALL and breached the floor. check-coverage.mjs
now enumerates each project's source files itself and sums per-file numbers into that
list, so an unloaded file contributes its full line count, all uncovered, and it fails
the run outright if any measured file is ever back to a zero line total. Note the
percentages are now 'share of source lines exercised' rather than executable-line
coverage; see the header of check-coverage.mjs for why, and do not compare them with
numbers from a tool that reports the latter.
FLOORS RE-BASELINED — 2026-08-06, against those honest denominators. Many dropped
sharply: collections 77 -> 33, administration 58 -> 29, ui 66 -> 40, nuxeo-client
76 -> 57. NONE OF THESE IS A REGRESSION OR A RELAXATION. No test was deleted and no
coverage was lost; the old numbers were measuring a subset of each project and
reporting it as the whole. collections' 77% was 445 covered lines out of the 1302 it
has, scored against a denominator that excluded its 766-line collection-detail.ts
because no spec loaded it. The new floors are the first ones that can be honestly
ratcheted, because writing the first spec for an untested file now raises the number
instead of lowering it.
Two projects were also never actually gated in CI: keys 'kd-client' and 'ke-client'
did not match their Nx project names, and CI filters by that name, so --projects=
never selected them. Renamed to shared-kd-client / shared-ke-client.
Three projects that had grown Vitest suites but no entry were added at the same time:
content-ports, content-adapter-nuxeo, and shared-ai-client, whose 'ungated' note
claimed it had no Nx targets at all — it has a test target and 100% line coverage.
shared-agent-client was added on the same basis: it had a Vitest suite and no floor.
It measures 90.41% lines / 96.20% functions under the honest denominator. The 97.11 /
97.02 recorded when the library was built were taken under the old gate and are not
comparable — the 6.7-point line gap is its untested agent.models.ts rejoining the
denominator, not lost coverage.
Branch coverage is deliberately not gated: several projects instrument too few
branch points for the percentage to mean anything (search reports 100% off 6
branches), so a branch floor would be noise rather than signal.
Function coverage is measured and printed but NOT enforced, and the recorded values
below are observations only. v8's empty report credits a file no spec loads with
exactly one function however large it is — an untested 766-line component reports one,
not forty. A line count can be corrected from the file itself; a function count cannot,
so a function floor would still carry the inverted incentive the line fix removed. Set
GATED_METRICS in check-coverage.mjs to re-enable it if that ever becomes measurable.
